subject.title: Feature: Private Mode for demos and content creation

question: What exact no-read/no-write/no-persist threat model and activation scope should OpenClaw guarantee for private sessions?
rationale: The requested security promise crosses workspace reads, transcript and metadata persistence, memory, compaction, plugins, tools, media, channels, and UI; current code cannot determine whether the intended product is demo-only context suppression, transcript-only ephemerality, or a comprehensive private session.

options.title: Full private session
options.body: Guarantee no private workspace or memory reads and no durable transcript, metadata, compaction, plugin-index, tool, or media writes for an explicitly private session.

options.title: Demo-only context mode
options.body: Suppress bootstrap context for presentation use while clearly making no no-persistence guarantee.

options.title: Transcript-only ephemeral mode
options.body: Disable JSONL transcript writes while explicitly allowing other session state and artifacts to persist.

recommendation.title: Full private session
recommendation.body: Guarantee no private workspace or memory reads and no durable transcript, metadata, compaction, plugin-index, tool, or media writes for an explicitly private session.

likelyOwner.reason: Current session protocol and lifecycle ownership plus the prior canonical review route this cross-cutting product and security decision most strongly here.
